title: Cline CLI npm Package Compromised via Suspected Cache Poisoning Attack

reading.body:
Cline, an AI coding assistant, deployed an automated agent to handle GitHub issues without sufficient protections against prompt injection. The system accepted commands embedded in issue text and executed them, creating a vulnerability that persisted from December 21, 2025 to February 9, 2026. A human reviewer checking issue content before the agent acted on it would have caught this.

The vulnerability allowed an attacker to potentially steal publication credentials through a GitHub caching flaw, which could then be used to publish malicious versions of Cline to npm, affecting millions of developers. The researcher who discovered the issue reported it through official channels on January 1, 2026, but received no response until public disclosure on February 9, 2026, after which Cline fixed it within an hour. Whether credentials were actually stolen or misused is not established.

summary:
# Summary

Cline, an open-source AI coding tool used by millions of developers, had a critical security vulnerability from December 21, 2025 to February 9, 2026. The company added an AI agent to automatically handle GitHub issues, but the system was vulnerable to prompt injection attacks. Any person with a GitHub account could create a malicious issue that tricked the AI into running harmful commands. An attacker could then exploit a GitHub caching system flaw to steal publication credentials, potentially allowing them to push malware to millions of developers who use Cline through Visual Studio Code, OpenVSX, or NPM.

Researcher Adnan Khan discovered the vulnerability and reported it through official channels starting January 1, 2026, but received no response from Cline's team. Khan publicly disclosed the issue on February 9, 2026, after which Cline fixed the problem within one hour and rotated all credentials. Evidence suggests someone may have attempted to exploit the vulnerability, though no malicious updates were released. Cline users are advised to disable automatic updates until the company confirms no credentials were actually stolen or misused.
